A1.justification: Both readable 11-page PDFs describe the same IAPL study, with corresponding equations, five figures and nine tables. Neither contains an appendix. V3 references separate supplementary details and experiments that are not supplied; no changes in that material can be inferred.

before.justification: V2 reports original IAPL evaluations on UniversalFakeDetect and GenImage, component ablations, and feature visualizations in Section 4.

after.justification: V3 retains the original IAPL experiments and ablations and additionally reports class-specific component results in Table 4.

M1.justification: The adapters, learnable tokens, conditional-information branches, entropy-based test-time tuning and final confidence-based selection remain unchanged. The scaling factor, general condition and Optimal Input Selection rename existing components; the corresponding equations and procedures are equivalent.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same cross-generator detection task on 19 UniversalFakeDetect subsets and eight GenImage subsets, training on ProGAN and SDv1.4 respectively. V3's four-class ProGAN caption adds documentation rather than establishing changed coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 replace Spec and F3Net with SAFE and MiraGe. Table 3 replaces DeiT-S and CO-SPY with ATTSD and MiraGe. SAFE remains a GenImage comparator, so its revised evaluation is not a newly added method there.

E3.justification: Table 3 replaces SAFE results cited from its original report with an explicitly marked SDv1.4 reimplementation. The added UniversalFakeDetect SAFE comparison uses its official pretrained model. IAPL's stated model, training budget, preprocessing, metrics and tuning settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 4 extends the existing component ablation with separate real and fake accuracies, allowing class-specific effects to be assessed. The component configurations, adapter-placement, token-layer, entropy-loss and tuning-step studies, and the visual analyses are otherwise retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations or significance tests. Prediction-confidence selection is retained and does not constitute statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: IAPL's benchmark scores and existing ablation values are unchanged. Comparator rows are replaced and Table 4 gains real/fake accuracy entries. SAFE's cited GenImage mAcc of 95.6% is replaced by 90.3% under the stated reimplementation, not an established same-setting decline. Section 4.3 replaces the erroneous 12/19 top-two mAP statement with 9/19 for mAcc, matching the updated Table 1.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 retain the same fusion, confidence and entropy definitions. Changes to condition subscripts and layer-index notation are equivalent notation; no assumptions, theoretical results or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain image-adaptive prompting, lightweight adaptation and generalization to unseen generators. The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same principal performance claims, including 95.61% and 96.7% mean accuracy.

C2.justification: V3 makes the adapter-placement interpretation more categorical, claiming six evenly spaced adapters outperform more layers, although Table 6 retains a tradeoff: eight layers have higher mAcc, while six have higher mAP. It also removes the brief limitation about weaker performance on certain generators.

D1.justification: V3 specifies four-class ProGAN training, explains the adapter configuration's start/end/interval notation, and identifies Nt as a layer count in Table 7. It removes the illustrative 1 × 10^-6 coefficient initialization. Core implementation settings, hardware and the code link remain unchanged; referenced supplementary CNN details are not provided.

R1.justification: V3 adds ATTSD, MiraGe and Frank et al.'s frequency-analysis work, and removes references associated with Spec, F3Net and DeiT-S. MiraGe also enters the introduction's comparison with fixed prompts. The broader positioning around CLIP adaptation and prompt learning remains intact.

P1.justification: Parts of the introduction and method explanations are rewritten or reordered, terminology is updated, and the entropy-ablation cross-reference is corrected from Table 5 to Table 8. Guoqing Xu is added to the author list. The overall section structure remains unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1, 3 and 4 are redrawn or relabeled, while Figures 2 and 5 retain their visual evidence. Table 4 gains real/fake accuracy columns, Table 5 moves below it, and page 8 is rearranged. Captions and headers are refined without changing the overall figure/table inventory.

improvement.justification: V3 makes the existing evidence easier to assess through explicit SAFE evaluation provenance, updated comparators, class-specific ablation results and corrected labels and references. These modest gains outweigh the loss of the brief limitation and initialization example. The benefit is limited by the overbroad Table 6 interpretation and unavailable referenced supplementary material; the method and headline results remain unchanged.
